not all hair care has to break you bank💰 1. brush starting at your ends and work your way up -starting at your ends helps remove tangles little by little instead of pulling one big knot through your entire strand. this puts a lot less tension on your hair, helps prevent unnecessary breakage, and is especially important if your hair is fine or prone to tangling. 2. scalp massages -i like to do a 5 to 10 minute scalp massage every day. this can help increase blood flow to the scalp, helps distribute your natural oils, and feels amazing. i personally do it because it’s great for overall scalp health and can support healthier, denser hair over time.  3. never sleep with wet hair -wet hair is at its weakest, so tossing and turning on a pillow all night creates extra friction that can lead to breakage, frizz, and split ends. it may seem convenient but in the long run it causes so much damage.  4. always split and rinse your hair after shampoo and conditioner -don’t just let the water run over the top of your head. separate your hair into sections and make sure you’re rinsing all the way down to your scalp and underneath your hair. leftover shampoo or conditioner can cause buildup, weigh your hair down, and even contribute to an itchy or irritated scalp. 5. wear protective hairstyles -protective styles help reduce friction, tangles, and unnecessary breakage throughout the day. i usually wear a very loose claw clip updo or a loose french braid. the key is keeping them loose, not tight. if your hairstyle is pulling on your scalp, it’s too tight. healthy hair isn’t about finding one miracle product. it’s all the little habits you stay consistent with that make the biggest difference over time💪🏻    #hair #haircare #healthyhair  #hairtips #kayliboyle

thick bakery style chocolate chip cookies🍪🍫 Ingredients: 170g (3/4 cup) unsalted butter, cold and cubed 150g (3/4 cup) brown sugar 70g (1/3 cup) granulated sugar 1 egg + 1 egg yolk 2 tsp vanilla 300g (2 1/2 cups) all purpose flour 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp baking powder 3/4 tsp salt 250g (1 1/2 cups) chocolate chips  Flakey sea salt (optional) Instructions:  1. In a large bowl, combine the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix until smooth and well combined. Do not cream. 2. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla, then mix until fully incorporated. 3. Add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt) and fold until just combined. 4. Fold in the chocolate chips or chunks until evenly distributed. Do not overmix. 5. Divide the dough into 150g portions and shape each into a rough ball. 6. Place the dough balls on a lined tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 7. Bake in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for 13-16 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are still slightly soft. 8. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. If desired, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and let cool for about 15 minutes before serving. Enjoy! Note: This recipe made 6 cookies weighing 150g each and 1 cookie weighing 100g🍪🤎 #baking #cookies #chocolatechipcookies #Recipe #nyccookies

top 5 tips to start your healthy hair care journey🌱✨ 1. cut off those split ends✂️      split ends can’t be repaired, only temporarily sealed. if you leave them, they can continue splitting farther up the hair shaft, leading to more breakage over time. regular trims help keep your hair looking thicker and healthier while preventing you from losing more length later. 2. do a 10 minute scalp massage daily💆🏼‍♀️      your scalp is skin, and healthy hair starts there. daily scalp massages can help increase blood flow to the scalp, reduce buildup, and create a healthier environment for your hair to grow. you can use your fingertips or a scalp massager. just be gentle and consistent. 3. start scalp + hair oiling🫶      find the right hair oil for your scalp and hair type because not every oil works for everyone. i oil my scalp for density, not to make my hair grow faster. massage it in for a few minutes 1 to 3 times a week before wash day, then wash it out after 3 to 4 hours if your scalp tolerates it well. i also have other videos that go into all the do’s and don’ts of hair oiling if you want to learn more. 4. get a blood panel done🩸      if your hair feels thinner than normal, sheds excessively, or isn’t growing like it used to, it may be worth asking your doctor for blood work. things like low iron, vitamin d, b12, zinc, or other deficiencies can affect hair health. if you’re deficient, focus on vitamin rich foods and only take supplements if recommended by your healthcare provider. 5. learn your hair before buying products🤍      figure out your hair pattern (straight, wavy, curly, or coily), strand texture (fine, medium, or coarse), porosity (how well your hair absorbs and holds moisture), and scalp type (oily, dry, balanced, or sensitive). once you know those, it’s much easier to build a routine that actually works for you instead of wasting money on products that aren’t a good fit. healthy hair isn’t about buying the most expensive products. it’s about understanding your hair, staying consistent, and being patient. 🤍   #haircare #healthyhair #HairCareTips #kayliboyle

Pt.4 | My fall bakery menu 🍂 Recipe below 👇🏼  Crumbl released their Dubai Chocolate Brownie, but why buy it when you can make an even better one at home? 🤎✨ Ingredients 🟤Brownie Base * 180g caster sugar * 2 eggs * 113g unsalted butter (for browning) * 170g chopped chocolate * 80g plain flour * 3 tbsp cocoa powder * ½ tsp salt 💚Kunafa Filling * 260g kunafa pastry (finely chopped) * 2 tbsp unsalted butter (for toasting kunafa) * 320g pistachio cream 🍫Chocolate Ganache * 120g double cream * 100g milk chocolate (chopped) Instructions 1. Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a baking pan with parchment paper. 2. Brown 113g of unsalted butter in a saucepan until golden, then set aside. 3. Melt the chopped chocolate in the microwave in short bursts until smooth, then stir in the browned butter and let cool slightly. 4. In a separate bowl, whisk the sugar and eggs until light and fluffy. 5. Add the chocolate butter mixture to the eggs and sugar, and whisk until fully combined. 6. Fold in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt until just incorporated. 7. Pour all of the brownie batter into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and bake for 22 minutes. Let cool completely in the pan. 8. In a pan over medium heat, melt 2 tbsp of butter. Add the finely chopped kunafa pastry and cook, stirring often, until golden and crisp. Let cool slightly. 9. Mix the toasted kunafa pastry with the pistachio cream until fully combined, then spread evenly over the cooled brownie. 10. Place the pan in the fridge for about 30 minutes to set. 11. For the ganache, place the double cream and chopped milk chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl. Heat in short bursts, stirring in between, until melted and glossy. 12. Pour the ganache over the pistachio-kunafa layer, spread evenly, and refrigerate, ideally overnight, or at least 1 hour before slicing. Enjoy! 🤎 #baking #dubaichocolate #brownies #Recipe #fall
